::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Does $P(X\leq a) = P(X^2\leq a^2)$ if $X$ is a positive random variable and $a>0$?](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/1104818/does-px-leq-a-px2-leq-a2-if-x-is-a-positive-random-variable-and-a0), asked by [Laimond](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/186742/laimond) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2015-01-15; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> The answer looks positive to me, since $$P(\omega:X(\omega) \leq a) = P(\omega:X(\omega)^2\leq a^2)$$
> Am I right?
:::

If $X(\omega) > 0$ for all $\omega$, and $a>0$, then
$$X(\omega)^2 \leq a^2 \iff X(\omega) \leq a$$
So as sets,
$$\{\omega : X(\omega)^2 \leq a^2\} = \{\omega :  X(\omega) \leq a\}$$
